figures.caption: Figure V1 — Wan2.2 TI2V-5B whole-clip denoising. The T2V worked example starts from a 31×44×80×48 latent tensor and patchifies it into 27,280 video tokens. The fetched implementation uses T_l=(F−1)//4+1, H_l=H//16 and W_l=W//16. For aligned F=4k+1, F=1+4(T_l−1): 31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames. The optional I2V branch is separate from the T2V budget. The feedback loop is denoising/scheduler iteration, not architectural recurrence. Fifty upstream timesteps use two CFG branch evaluations each. The VAE decode is not autoregressive text decode. [1P][FACT] geometry and loop; [1P][DERIVED] aligned inverse and token count. Schematic, not a latency or peak-memory measurement.
figures.alt_text: Prompt encoding, labeled at most 512 prompt tokens, and optional reference-image VAE encoding condition a whole-clip denoising block. Initial FP32 latent noise enters from the right. The feedback loop is labeled denoising / scheduler iteration. The VAE stride is temporal 4 and spatial 16 by 16. The aligned endpoint formula 1+4 times (31 minus 1) gives 121 output frames at 1280 by 704 pixels and 24 frames per second. Solid data/state arrows and dashed conditioning arrows are distinct without color.

figures.caption: Figure V2 — Wan2.2 A14B selects experts as the denoising schedule progresses. The stage-transition arrow spans timestep evaluations; it does not chain both experts inside one forward evaluation. Each expert is stored in its respective checkpoint. Both occupy GPU weight memory only if both remain on GPU; only the selected expert runs in a branch evaluation. Official rounded counts are about 27B total and about 14B active, not an inferred per-expert parameter split. Stage widths are schematic and do not encode step counts. Explicit offload changes residency and adds transfers. This is a different model from the dense 5B example. [1P][FACT].
figures.alt_text: A blue resident-bank outline encloses high-noise and low-noise expert checkpoints. Dashed links connect each checkpoint to its stage. Text labels progress across the denoising schedule and states that two experts do not run within one forward evaluation. A rightward stage arrow joins high-noise to low-noise processing across timesteps. About 14 billion parameters are active per evaluation; about 27 billion are GPU-resident only if both experts remain on GPU. Stage widths do not encode step counts. Offload adds weight transfers.
